how: An alum initiates the Big Ten N project by supplying specifications and asking why the room has not acted.
The specifications post calls for a Northwestern presence and the completion post renews the call as maintenance.
Participants identify too little space for an added word or stripe, rather than too few hands to sustain the existing N.
The room finds an existing N, hears how people made it, and receives a further lettering proposal.
Members propose additions and dispute whether expansion will fit or expose the N to hijacking.
The organiser reports completion together with requests to maintain the N.
Coordinates, a specification sheet, and a direct canvas bookmark make the work locatable and reproducible.
After revising a shared design to spare a neighbour, participants must erase obsolete pixels and redirect helpers to the updated sheet.
Short greetings and praise do not demonstrate bare acceptance of a call, and acceptance through silent placing remains unseen.
Completion requests and an attack alert show no scripts, bots, or spare accounts, without establishing that none were used.
One room cannot test cross-room prevalence, and initiative or shaming outsiders does not establish whether formal internal order was decided.
The organiser explicitly prioritises maintaining and rebuilding the N over attacking neighbouring schools.
Warnings about battles and an attack alert rally attention to protecting the N.
A supposed attack is diagnosed as the room erasing its own obsolete column during a planned move.
Participants identify suspected defacers, receive a misclick explanation, and report a private-message account of deliberate redesign.
Defenders solicit named repeat offenders and invoke public shaming in their college communities as leverage beyond direct pixel repair.
Neighbouring builders clarify the northeast edge and the pixels to which a border will extend.
The organiser explicitly moves the N one square to avoid impinging on Purdue.
The organiser tells participants not to attack neighbours and to contact unwanted tile placers instead.
Neighbour accommodation can require a small move and removal of the old column without abandoning a defeated position.
The first N's reported loss and a later Big Ten project do not establish that defeat prompted a coordinated relocation.
An alum asks this room to help Chicago's flag, with no coded response establishing delivered help.
A neighbour's greeting and the organiser's reciprocal compliment instantiate courtesy without demonstrating an exchange of pixels.
Notification of the neighbouring room is suggested, but a completed envoy mission is not reported.
Sharing a league corner and exchanging greetings do not establish a mutual-defence coalition.
An objection that nearby space is claimed does not establish a guest work governed by a territorial host.
Border clarification and suggested notification do not dispute who can commit the room to an agreement.
A league pun imports school belonging into skeptical joking, without establishing a pre-existing quarrel or allegiance to a colour faction.
A participant explicitly offers school spirit as one reason to make the N.
Attributing damage to school fans does not establish that a quarrel predating the canvas was carried into it.
The strike exhortation names no rival and the conditional reference to attacking the jug does not clearly establish a rivalry-driven attack call.
Questioning why the group makes the N elicits a justification of the effort's worth rather than an assessment of its strength.
Naming Reddit's April Fools project does not establish that the host room itself staged a fake or takeover.
Completion announcements and praise publicly mark the N as a shared accomplishment.
A maker recounts the early N's loss and values its saved screenshot well before closure.
Completion and the final coded joke do not show reuse of the mark or continuation into another canvas.
The early screenshot recollection and the last pre-close joke cannot test a post-placement dispute over the retained version.
Expansionist exhortation and a proposed checkerboard supply attack or encroachment talk, while actual execution remains unverified.
Participants carry the conflict into accusations, a misclick apology, and a report of deliberate white-on-white redesign.
The misclick apology receives skeptical joking that ends in a league pun.
The initiating call and later completion show a compatible sequence without independently demonstrating that the call recruited the people who built.
The alum's initiation and appeal occupy one passage, leaving the proposed starter-to-call mechanism inseparable in this record.
The completed-N announcement explicitly makes maintenance the next task.
Border negotiation can arise from construction overlap rather than erosion of an already maintained mark.
The organiser links the revised one-square placement to sparing Purdue, without requiring a formal treaty.
An attack and a rebuilding instruction do not establish whether strain led members to machine placements.
The completion report is itself a public announcement and receives visible praise in the build thread.
Credit, loss, and screenshot appreciation coexist in one early recollection without showing that celebration caused recording.
A saved screenshot and near-close joke supply no visible decision to continue the effort after recording it.
Insufficient space for an extra word is not evidence that too few hands forced relocation of the existing mark.
Revised specifications are visible, but the edited post cannot establish the exact timing of design agreement and template publication.
Praise after a build call does not test bare joining, and joining through unreported placements cannot be inspected.
An outside-help appeal and neighbour greetings do not establish maintenance strain, insufficient hands, and subsequent delivery of help.
Courtesy following border discussion does not demonstrate a bargain trading space for upkeep or protection.
Recruitment precedes aggressive proposals, but no concept links recruitment causally to those proposals.
A room can reject a proposed design addition to prevent a neighbour hijacking it before an explicit raid or retaliation begins.
The organiser answers discussion of claiming adjacent space with an explicit reason to rebuild rather than attack others.
The expansion proposals do not visibly elicit a treaty invocation or a new border negotiation.
Accusations concerning damage to the N do not establish that the room's own targetless strike exhortation caused the ensuing rivalry talk.
An earlier greeting and later attack alert do not establish defence strain leading to coalition membership.
A participation-worth exchange can occur without a post flood or a demand to contain canvas talk.
Border discussion is visible without a subsequent dispute over whose agreement binds other placers.
Accommodating a neighbour returns the build to revised shared instructions, making template use iterative rather than a one-way settlement.
